web_evidence.title: Writing Styles in Table For Two
web_evidence.note: The structural analysis explicitly maps 'The Line' and 'The Ballad of Timothy Touchett' to omniscient third person; four New York stories to first person; and 'Eve in Hollywood' to third person with shifting character perspectives.

web_evidence.title: Table for Two — Penguin Books authorized sample
web_evidence.note: The publisher's sustained authorized excerpt of 'The Line' narrates Pushkin and Irina externally in third person across many pages.

web_evidence.title: Table for Two: Q and A — Amor Towles
web_evidence.note: Towles identifies Mary Elizabeth Harkness as the narrator of 'The Bootlegger,' calls Percy the narrator of 'The DiDomenico Fragment,' and describes the former narrator hearing the culminating cello performance; this primary-source account corroborates autonomous participating narrators in named stories.

person_note: This prose collection has sustained components in different narrative persons, so ALTERNATING applies at book level. The quoted 'we' from 'The Bootlegger' exposes a participating first-person witness, while the Timothy Touchett passage and authorized Penguin sample expose third-person narration. A commercial whole-book guide maps four stories to first person and two stories plus the novella to third person; Towles's Q&A corroborates named first-person narrators. Confidence is medium because the source that supplies the complete component-by-component map is commercial, not Tier B.
